question: While CD sales are currently showing signs of growth, many consumers have expressed frustration at the disappearance of CD players from new vehicles. At the same time, the European automotive market appears to be moving towards the full digitalisation of music and entertainment media.

In addition to cultural disadvantages, including discrimination of smaller languages, limited access to rarer titles and potentially lower incomes for artists, this development also raises legitimate road safety concerns, as navigating through infotainment system touchscreens may cause greater visual and cognitive distraction than operating the vehicle controls.

Against this backdrop, concerns have been raised about the unintended consequences of the EU General Safety Regulation II (GSR II). In particular, its implementation has contributed to the discontinuation of certain equipment, including CD players, affecting the marketability of vehicles still equipped with such systems. 1.
Does the Commission intend to assess whether, and to what extent, GSR II has contributed to the disappearance of CD players from new vehicles?
Was this an intended or foreseeable consequence of GSR II?
Does the Commission intend to ensure that consumers can retain a CD player as an optional feature when acquiring a new vehicle, including by amending GSR II?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.11.2026) Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 (GSR II)1 lays down technical requirements for new vehicles regarding their general safety and the protection of vehicle occupants and vulnerable road users. It requires each new vehicle to be equipped with advanced safety systems such as the driver drowsiness and attention warning and the driver distraction warning systems.

Navigation infotainment systems, including audio-visual equipment are optional vehicle equipment. CD players have never been mandatory in vehicles. Thus, it is the choice of the manufacturer whether to provide such equipment, against payment or free of charge, and in which vehicle models.

The Commission is not aware of the existence of any causal link between the implementation of the GSR II and the discontinuation of certain vehicle equipment. Moreover, there is no compelling evidence that the use of vehicle infotainment systems with touchscreens causes greater visual and cognitive distraction compared to other technologies like CD players with physical control buttons.
The Commission has no plans for legislative amendments to mandate CD players in vehicles.
1 Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 November 2019 on type-

approval requirements for motor vehicles and their trailers, and systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, as regards their general safety and the protection of vehicle occupants and vulnerable road users (OJ L 325, 16.12.2019, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2019/2144/oj).
